newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian party received cash from Dassault - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian party received cash from Dassault - paper.

text.p: A Belgian newspaper said on Tuesday the Flemish Christian Democratic Party (CVP), now led by Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, was given 1.2 million francs ($40,000) by French aerospace firm Dassault in 1987.

The daily De Morgen said the independent Oversight Committee had given the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, a report saying the money was passed over in December 1987 when Wilfried Martens headed the then Christian Democrat-Liberal coalition.
No comment was immediately obtainable from the CVP.
It is not the first time Dassault's name has been connected with money allegedly paid to Belgian political parties, but it is the first time it has been connected with the CVP.

NATO Secretary General Willy Claes, a government economics minister for the Socialist Party in the late 1980s, was forced to resign in October last year over bribes alleged to have been paid to his party by Dassault and Italian helicopter maker Agusta in exchange for for contracts.
Another Socialist minister at the time, Guy Coeme, was also forced to quit 18 months ago for the same reasons.
A series of Christian Democrat-Socialist governments have held power since early 1988.
In May this year Belgium issued an international arrest warrant for company head Serge Dassault on suspicion of corruption.
He has denied allegations he paid 10 million francs ($2 million) in bribes for a deal to modernise Belgian air force F16 and Mirage fighter jets.
